sources: Headless replay from power-on: each of the seven chapters started in turn and made to draw every code it has, and the drawn glyphs matched against the chapter's font from the disc

The 1,153 kanji and Latin glyphs read by eye, then checked by decoding every scene's script from the disc against a word list (nine readings corrected); the 18 codes no scene uses are read by eye only
The chapter byte found by comparing memory at each chapter's first scene
The two wait codes and the script position seen in a replay of chapter 6's first scene: 60 presses through three scripts, the position compared with the script at each stop

Ten Genkan snapshots of real play in chapter 5 (two conversations, then walking): both scripts decode with no unmapped code, and the chapter's layout reads the page on screen in each (no text in the four taken while walking)

The seven chapter programs (CAP5.EXE to CAPH.EXE): each keeps the same cells at its own addresses, found by matching the code around chapter 5's. Which command words take an argument word is read from the script interpreter's code, the same in all seven; the words in use, from every scene's script
notes: 16-bit little-endian codes, not Tansaku-hen's (SLPS-00102): 0x0000-0x00DB are shared; kanji are 0x00DC up, numbered anew by each chapter. Each chapter is its own program with its cells elsewhere: one layout per program, told apart by the word at 0x80041C78, each with its chapter's table. The script at 0x801FE800 is one record at a time. The message is the page so far (the window shows its last rows). A choice's answers are rows of it, each after a colon; the game draws their letters and waits up to five words past the end code. Waiting is true for a frame or two after an answer is taken.
